problem: Nova needed a packaging supplier for a new moisturizer line (250ml PET jars, 40K unit initial run).
reason: Alpha offered 9% lower unit cost and a shorter quoted lead time (18 days vs 26 days) at the required MOQ.
outcome: Order placed; onboarding completed without issue.

problem: First scheduled delivery from Supplier Alpha for the moisturizer line arrived late.
options_considered: Accept delay and adjust production schedule
decision_made: Escalated to Alpha account manager; production schedule shifted by 12 days.
reason: Delay of 12 days against the confirmed delivery window caused a near-stockout on retail shelves for two SKUs.
outcome: Alpha attributed the delay to a raw material shortage on their end; committed to improved scheduling going forward.

problem: A second Alpha delivery for Nova's moisturizer line arrived 18 days late, this time without advance notice.
options_considered: Request formal remediation plan from Alpha
Begin sourcing an alternate vendor in parallel
decision_made: Requested formal remediation plan and began parallel sourcing conversations as a contingency.
reason: Two delays within four months, the second unannounced, was treated as a pattern rather than a one-off.
outcome: Alpha proposed a revised production slot and a dedicated line, but could not commit to a firm delivery guarantee.

problem: Alpha's remediation plan did not include a firm delivery guarantee ahead of Nova's Q1 restock cycle.
options_considered: Continue with Alpha on a probationary basis
Switch to Coastal Pack Co. for the moisturizer line
decision_made: Switched packaging for the moisturizer line to Coastal Pack Co.
reason: Restock timing was considered too critical to risk a third delay; Coastal Pack Co. offered a shorter, more predictable lead time despite a ~6% higher unit cost.
outcome: Transition completed over 5 weeks; no further delivery issues reported for this SKU line since the switch.

problem: Verve's marketing team proposed the label claim 'clinically proven to boost immunity' for a new wellness drink SKU.
decision_made: Rejected the claim as written; approved revised language 'formulated with immunity-supporting ingredients.'
reason: No clinical trial data existed to support 'clinically proven'; the claim carried regulatory risk under advertising standards.
outcome: Revised copy approved and used on final packaging; no regulatory issues raised post-launch.

problem: Lumen planned the go-to-market approach for a new premium diffuser line.
options_considered: Retail-first launch with digital as secondary support
decision_made: Digital-only launch via influencer partnerships, no retail distribution in phase 1.
reason: Lower upfront cost, faster time-to-market, and the product's premium positioning was assessed to fit a digital-savvy early-adopter audience; retail listing fees and lead time were seen as slowing launch speed.
outcome: Launched February 2026; see D07 for post-launch retrospective.

problem: 90-day retrospective on the diffuser line's digital-only launch, against original forecast.
options_considered: Continue digital-only and extend influencer spend
decision_made: Added limited retail distribution for the line starting month 4; retained digital as primary channel.
reason: 60-day sales reached 61% of forecast; 90-day sales reached 68% of forecast. Awareness surveys showed strong recognition within existing digital-savvy segments but minimal penetration outside them. Reorder rate was 22% versus a projected 35%, attributed partly to lack of in-store discovery and trial.
outcome: Retail addition improved awareness metrics over the following quarter; retrospective lesson documented for future launches: digital-only channel concentration limits reach beyond the existing digital audience and slows trial-driven reorder for premium home goods.

problem: Kindle needed flexible packaging (foil pouches) for a new snack SKU line.
reason: Alpha's flexible packaging line (distinct production line from bottle/jar packaging) had strong on-time performance for Kindle's product category and volume tier.
outcome: Three delivery cycles completed on schedule; no issues reported to date.

problem: Kindle needed a raw ingredient supplier for a new protein bar's whey protein isolate component.
reason: Beta offered competitive pricing at volume and a documented quality certification for the specific ingredient grade required.
outcome: Consistent quality and on-time delivery across four sourcing cycles; relationship considered stable.

problem: A batch of Verve's wellness drink sourced from Supplier Beta triggered an internal quality hold pending investigation of a possible contamination signal in a probiotic ingredient.
decision_made: Quarantined the affected batch and conducted targeted retesting; no recall issued.
reason: Retesting on a statistically representative sample did not confirm contamination beyond acceptable thresholds, but the source batch could not be fully cleared with high confidence given testing limitations, and the affected units were destroyed as a precaution.
outcome: No confirmed contamination in retested samples; Beta relationship continued with additional incoming QA checks added for this ingredient category specifically.

problem: Supplier Gamma, Nova's co-packing partner for a seasonal gift-set SKU, signaled a capacity constraint ahead of the holiday production window.
options_considered: Wait for Gamma's existing line to free up
Request Gamma add a secondary production line
Source a second co-packer for overflow volume
decision_made: Requested Gamma add a secondary production line for the season.
reason: Gamma had sufficient facility capacity to add a line with two weeks' notice, avoiding the cost and onboarding time of a new co-packer relationship.
outcome: Secondary line added on schedule; seasonal volume produced without delay.

problem: Aura's existing service-level agreement with Supplier Gamma for contract manufacturing was up for renewal, with Gamma proposing a revised minimum order commitment.
decision_made: Negotiated a lower MOQ threshold with a modest per-unit price increase.
reason: Aura's SKU velocity did not support the originally proposed MOQ without excess inventory risk.
outcome: Revised terms signed; relationship continued without disruption.

problem: Aura sought a lower unit cost from Supplier Beta for a shared raw ingredient used across two SKUs.
decision_made: Negotiated a 6% volume-based discount by combining forecasted demand across the two SKUs.
reason: Beta offered tiered pricing once combined forecasted volume crossed a threshold.
outcome: Discount applied to subsequent purchase orders; no quality or delivery issues reported.

problem: Verve needed a glass bottle supplier for a premium cold-pressed juice line.
reason: Alpha's glass packaging division (separate from its PET line) quoted competitive pricing and had prior experience with premium beverage clients.
outcome: Deliveries on schedule across five production cycles; no issues reported.

problem: Kindle's marketing team proposed the claim 'high in protein' for a new snack bar SKU.
options_considered: Approve claim as written pending lab verification
decision_made: Approved the claim following lab verification confirming protein content met the regulatory threshold for 'high in protein' labeling.
reason: Lab results were provided and met the applicable regulatory definition, unlike unsubstantiated efficacy claims.
outcome: Claim used on final packaging; no issues raised post-launch.

problem: Nova evaluated expanding an existing skincare SKU line into additional regional retail chains.
options_considered: Hold current retail footprint and focus on e-commerce growth
decision_made: Expanded to 2 additional regional retail chains.
reason: Existing retail presence showed strong sell-through rates, and the SKU line already had established brand awareness in-region.
outcome: Sell-through in new chains met forecast within the first quarter.

problem: Lumen needed a glass jar supplier for its core scented candle line.
reason: Alpha's glass division offered a design customization option the incumbent vendor could not match within the required timeline.
outcome: Deliveries on schedule across all cycles to date; no issues reported.

problem: Supplier Gamma's co-packing ramp-up for a new Kindle snack SKU fell behind the agreed onboarding schedule by 9 days.
options_considered: Extend timeline and continue with Gamma
decision_made: Escalated for expedited resourcing; timeline extended by 9 days.
reason: Gamma attributed the delay to onboarding a new production line for the SKU's format; no prior performance issues existed with Gamma for Kindle.
outcome: Line completed onboarding 9 days behind original schedule; launch date shifted accordingly; no further delays since.
